questions.question: What components make up the Day 120 Capstone AI Data Assistant?
options: A single LLM API call with a detailed prompt
RAG pipeline + SQL agent + semantic caching + guardrails + evaluation pipeline
A fine-tuned model with a web interface
A vector database with a search UI
questions.explanation: The capstone integrates all Phase 10 skills: RAG for knowledge retrieval, a SQL agent for data queries, semantic caching for cost optimization, guardrails for safety, and an evaluation pipeline for quality monitoring — demonstrating full-stack LLM engineering.

questions.question: What is the purpose of query routing in the capstone system?
options: Load balancing across multiple servers
An orchestrator determines whether a question should use RAG (knowledge) or an agent (data queries)
DNS routing for API calls
Distributing training data across GPUs
questions.explanation: The orchestrator classifies incoming questions: 'What is our refund policy?' routes to RAG (policy knowledge base), while 'What was last quarter's revenue?' routes to the SQL agent (database queries). This ensures each question type uses the best retrieval strategy.

questions.question: What should a production monitoring dashboard track for an LLM system?
options: Only the number of API calls per day
Latency, cost per query, cache hit rate, RAGAS quality scores, and error rates
Only the user satisfaction scores
Only the model's training loss curve
questions.explanation: A production LLM dashboard should track operational metrics (latency, error rate, cache hit rate), cost metrics (tokens consumed, cost per query), and quality metrics (RAGAS faithfulness, answer relevancy). Alerts on any degradation enable proactive issue resolution.

questions.question: Why does the capstone require both a model card and a responsible deployment checklist?
options: They're optional nice-to-haves for documentation
The model card documents capabilities/limitations; the checklist ensures safety/compliance steps are completed before launch
They're required by OpenAI's terms of service
They replace the need for technical testing
questions.explanation: The model card documents what the system can and cannot do, its known limitations, and performance across demographics. The responsible deployment checklist ensures all safety steps (guardrails, bias audit, privacy review, monitoring) are completed before going live.

questions.question: What is the most important lesson from building a full-stack LLM application?
options: The largest model always produces the best results
Prompt engineering alone is sufficient for production systems
Production AI requires integration of multiple techniques: retrieval, caching, guardrails, evaluation, and monitoring
Open-source models should always be preferred over APIs
questions.explanation: No single technique makes a production LLM system. Real-world AI applications require thoughtful integration of RAG for knowledge, caching for cost, guardrails for safety, evaluation for quality, and monitoring for reliability — each solving different aspects of the production challenge.
